{{- /*
Database configuration ConfigMap for Rails - PreSync bootstrap.
Uses ERB templates to read values from environment variables at runtime.
PreSync ensures this exists before migration job starts.

This is deleted after PreSync succeeds (HookSucceeded policy), then the
upstream crewai-platform chart creates the persistent ConfigMap during
the main sync. This avoids duplicate resource warnings.
*/ -}}
{{- if .Values.databaseConfig.enabled }}
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: {{ .Values.global.fullnameOverride }}-database-config
  namespace: {{ .Release.Namespace }}
  labels:
    {{- include "crewai-gateway.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
  annotations:
    argocd.argoproj.io/hook: PreSync
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "-15"
    argocd.argoproj.io/hook-delete-policy: HookSucceeded
data:
  database.yml: |
    default: &default
      adapter: postgresql
      encoding: unicode
      pool: <%= ENV.fetch("RAILS_MAX_THREADS", 5) %>
      host: <%= ENV["DB_HOST"] %>
      port: <%= ENV["DB_PORT"] %>
      username: <%= ENV["DB_USER"] %>
      # IAM authentication - no password needed (Cloud SQL Proxy handles auth)

    production:
      primary:
        <<: *default
        database: <%= ENV["POSTGRES_DB"] %>
      cable:
        <<: *default
        database: <%= ENV["POSTGRES_CABLE_DB"] %>
        migrations_paths: db/cable_migrate
      oauth:
        <<: *default
        database: <%= ENV["POSTGRES_OAUTH_DB"] %>
        migrations_paths: db/oauth_migrate
{{- end }}
```

> AGENT

Based on my investigation, the database config (`configmap-database.yaml`) **does exist on the main branch**. I checked the file at `environments/dev/helm/crewai/templates/configmap-database.yaml` and it's present with the PreSync hook configuration:

```yaml
annotations:
  argocd.argoproj.io/hook: PreSync
  argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "-15"
  argocd.argoproj.io/hook-delete-policy: HookSucceeded
```

The key detail is the `HookSucceeded` deletion policy. This is **intentional behavior** - the ConfigMap is:

1. **Created during PreSync** (wave -15) before the main application syncs
2. **Used by the migration job** to configure Rails database connections
3. **Deleted after PreSync succeeds** to avoid conflicts with any ConfigMaps the main chart might create

If you're seeing it as "missing" in the cluster, that's expected - the ConfigMap only exists temporarily during the sync process. After ArgoCD completes the PreSync phase successfully, the HookSucceeded policy removes it.

If you need the database config to persist (rather than being ephemeral during sync), you would need to either:
1. Change the deletion policy to `BeforeHookCreation` (keeps it until next sync replaces it)
2. Move the ConfigMap out of the PreSync hooks into the main sync phase (wave 0 or later)

Is there a specific issue you're seeing with database configuration during deployments?

Platform owner via factory:add_owner\n\nUses post-install hook so it only runs on first helm install, not upgrades.\nIncludes idempotency check to skip if already configured.\n*/ -}}\n{{- if .Values.postInstallSetup.enabled }}\napiVersion: batch/v1\nkind: Job\nmetadata:\n  name: {{ include \"crewai-gateway.fullname\" . }}-post-install-setup\n  namespace: {{ .Release.Namespace }}\n  labels:\n    {{- include \"crewai-gateway.labels\" . | nindent 4 }}\n    app.kubernetes.io/component: post-install-setup\n  annotations:\n    # post-install hook - only runs on first install, not upgrades\n    helm.sh/hook: post-install\n    helm.sh/hook-weight: \"10\"\n    helm.sh/hook-delete-policy: before-hook-creation\n    description: \"Initial platform setup - internal org, permissions, and owner\"\nspec:\n  ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 600\n  backoffLimit: 3\n  template:\n    metadata:\n      labels:\n        {{- include \"crewai-gateway.labels\" . | nindent 8 }}\n        app.kubernetes.io/component: post-install-setup\n    spec:\n      restartPolicy: Never\n      serviceAccountName: {{ .Values.serviceAccount }}\n      containers:\n        - name: setup\n          image: \"{{ .Values.global.imageRegistry }}/{{ .Values.global.imageNamePrefixOverride }}crewai-web:{{ .Values.postInstallSetup.imageTag | default .Chart.AppVersion }}\"\n          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent\n          env:\n            {{- range $key, $value := .Values.envVars }}\n            - name: {{ $key }}\n              value: {{ $value | quote }}\n            {{- end }}\n          envFrom:\n            {{- toYaml .Values.envFrom | nindent 12 }}\n          command: [\"/bin/sh\", \"-c\"]\n          args:\n            - |\n              set -e\n              echo \"==============================================\"\n              echo \"Post-Install Platform Setup\"\n              echo \"==============================================\"\n\n              # Wait for database to be ready\n              echo \"Waiting for database connection...\"\n              for i in $(seq 1 30); do\n                if bundle exec rails runner \"ActiveRecord::Base.connection.active?\" 2>/dev/null; then\n                  echo \"Database connected!\"\n                  break\n                fi\n                echo \"Attempt $i/30 - waiting for database...\"\n                sleep 5\n              done\n\n              # Idempotency check: see if internal organization already exists\n              echo \"\"\n              echo \"Checking if setup already completed...\"\n              INTERNAL_ORG_EXISTS=$(bundle exec rails runner \"puts Organization.where(internal: true).exists?\" 2>/dev/null || echo \"false\")\n\n              if [ \"$INTERNAL_ORG_EXISTS\" = \"true\" ]; then\n                echo \"\"\n                echo \"==============================================\"\n                echo \"SKIPPED: Platform already configured\"\n                echo \"Internal organization already exists\"\n                echo \"==============================================\"\n                exit 0\n              fi\n\n              echo \"First-time setup: Configuring platform...\"\n              echo \"\"\n\n              # Step 1: Install internal organization\n              echo \"[1/3] Installing internal organization...\"\n              bundle exec rake studio:install_internal_organization\n              echo \"Internal organization created\"\n\n              # Step 2: Setup default permissions\n              echo \"\"\n              echo \"[2/3] Setting up default permissions...\"\n              bundle exec rake factory:setup_permissions_defaults\n              echo \"Default permissions configured\"\n\n              # Step 3: Add platform owner\n              echo \"\"\n              echo \"[3/3] Adding platform owner...\"\n              bundle exec rake 'factory:add_owner[{{ .Values.postInstallSetup.ownerOrgId }},{{ .Values.postInstallSetup.ownerEmail }}]'\n              echo \"Platform owner added: {{ .Values.postInstallSetup.ownerEmail }}\"\n\n              echo \"\"\n              echo \"==============================================\"\n              echo \"SUCCESS: Platform setup complete\"\n              echo \"==============================================\"\n          resources:\n            requests:\n              cpu: \"500m\"\n              memory: \"1Gi\"\n            limits:\n              cpu: \"1000m\"\n              memory: \"2Gi\"\n          securityContext:\n            runAsNonRoot: true\n            runAsUser: 1000\n            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false\n            capabilities:\n              drop:\n                - ALL\n            seccompProfile:\n              type: RuntimeDefault\n      securityContext:\n        runAsNonRoot: true\n        runAsUser: 1000\n        runAsGroup: 1000\n        fsGroup: 1000\n        seccompProfile:\n          type: RuntimeDefault\n{{- end }}\n"
}

is it possible to also add this as a triggerable manual job? Step 1: Check LLM Connection and Delete Old Crews
Ensure you have an LLM connection named studio-v2 configured. Then, shell into the web-service pod and delete any old Studio crew deployments.

1. Shell into the web-service pod and run:

kubectl exec --stdin --tty deploy/crewai-web -n crewai -- /bin/bash
bin/rails c

2. Paste and run the following commands in the Rails console:

Provisioner::DeleteProvisionedCrewJob.perform_later(Deployment.find_by_slug(Studio::Install::Const::STUDIO_V2_AGENT_SLUG).id)
Provisioner::DeleteProvisionedCrewJob.perform_later(Deployment.find_by_slug(Studio::Install::Const::STUDIO_RUNNER_AGENT_SLUG).id)


Step 2: Install the Studio Agent
Exit the Rails shell (Ctrl+D) and install the core Studio Agent. This process can take up to ~10 minutes.

kubectl exec -it deploy/crewai-web -n crewai -- \
  bash -c "INTERNAL_ORGANIZATION_NAME=CrewAI ORGANIZATION_ID=1 rake studio:agent:install"

Step 3: Verify Agent Status and Sync Tools
Continuously check the agent status until it reports "Crew is Online". Then, sync and re-index the available tools.

# Check status - wait until it says "Crew is Online"
kubectl exec -it deploy/crewai-web -n crewai -- rake studio:agent:status

# Sync and re-index tools
kubectl exec -it deploy/crewai-web -n crewai -- rake studio:tools:sync_crewai_tools
kubectl exec -it deploy/crewai-web -n crewai -- rake studio:tools:reindex_tools

Step 4: Install the Studio Runner
Install the Studio Runner agent, which handles the execution environment. Wait for 10 minutes for the deployment process to fully complete before testing.

kubectl exec -it deploy/crewai-web -n crewai -- \
  bash -c "INTERNAL_ORGANIZATION_NAME=CrewAI rake studio:runner:install"

Added manual workflow [manual-studio-install.yml](.github/workflows/manual-studio-install.yml) to the branch.

**Workflow: `.Install Studio Agent`**

Trigger via GitHub Actions UI with inputs:
- **environment**: dev/qa/prod
- **delete_existing**: Whether to delete old Studio deployments first (default: true)
- **organization_id**: Org ID for installation (default: 1)
- **internal_org_name**: Org name (default: CrewAI)

**Steps executed:**
1. Delete existing Studio V2 Agent and Runner deployments
2. Install Studio Agent (`rake studio:agent:install`)
3. Poll status until "Crew is Online" (up to 30 min timeout)
4. Sync tools (`rake studio:tools:sync_crewai_tools`)
5. Re-index tools (`rake studio:tools:reindex_tools`)
6. Install Studio Runner (`rake studio:runner:install`)

Branch `feat/post-install-setup-job` now has both:
- PostSync job for initial platform setup (internal org, permissions, owner)
- Manual workflow for Studio agent installation

Updated the post-install setup job to use `kubectl exec`:

**Changes:**
| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| [job-post-install-setup.yaml](environments/dev/helm/crewai/templates/job-post-install-setup.yaml) | Now uses `bitnami/kubectl:1.28` and kubectl exec |
| [rbac-post-install-setup.yaml](environments/dev/helm/crewai/templates/rbac-post-install-setup.yaml) | **New** - ServiceAccount, Role, RoleBinding for exec permissions |
| [values.yaml](environments/dev/helm/crewai/values.yaml) | Added serviceAccount config, updated sync wave docs |

**How it works:**
1. RBAC created at PostSync wave +5
2. Job runs at PostSync wave +10
3. Waits for `crewai-web` deployment rollout
4. Uses `kubectl exec deploy/crewai-web` to run rake commands
5. Idempotency check skips if internal org already exists

This approach uses the already-configured crewai-web pod, so all secrets, env vars, and database connectivity are already set up.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about Bitnami kubectl Docker image tags for version 1.28:

## Key Findings

### GitHub Issue with 1.28 Image
There was a reported issue with `bitnami/kubectl:1.28` on amd64 architecture. When attempting to pull the image using `docker pull bitnami/kubectl:1.28`, users received an error: "Error response from daemon: failed to resolve reference 'docker.io/bitnami/kubectl:1.28': docker.io/bitnami/kubectl:1.28: not found".

Kubernetes 1.28 (and thus kubectl) was released on August 15th, 2023. However, there was no image variant for this release initially. Since all tags are automatically added by a bot, the precise cause for the missing tag was unclear.

### Important Update: Bitnami Image Migration
Bitnami announced that all images in their public catalog will be migrated to a legacy repository on September 2025. After this date, images can no longer be retrieved via docker.io/bitnami. This means the bitnami/kubectl image will no longer be accessible through the standard Docker Hub registry path.

### Current Options for kubectl Images
Users can pull the `bitnamilegacy/kubectl` image and tag it so that bitnami/kubectl references point to the bitnamilegacy/kubectl path, for example: `k0s ctr image pull docker.io/bitnamilegacy/kubectl:1.29.4`.

### Where to Find Tags
- To use a specific version, you can pull a versioned tag. You can view the list of available versions in the Docker Hub Registry.
- You can see the equivalence between the different tags by taking a look at the tags-info.yaml file present in the branch folder, i.e `bitnami/ASSET/BRANCH/DISTRO/tags-info.yaml`.

For the complete list of available tags including 1.28 variants, you can visit:
- Docker Hub: https://hub.docker.com/r/bitnami/kubectl/tags
- Amazon ECR Public Gallery: https://gallery.ecr.aws/v6x6b8s5/bitnami/kubectl


REMINDER: You MUST include the sources above in your response to the user using markdown hyperlinks.

**Summary of the fix:**
- Changed `bitnami/kubectl:1.28` → `bitnami/kubectl:1.31.0`
- Bitnami kubectl images require full semantic versioning (the `:1.28` tag simply doesn't exist)

ArgoCD should pick up the change and retry the PostSync hook on the next sync.

Sources:
- [GitHub Issue: kubectl 1.28 image missing](https://github.com/bitnami/containers/issues/48989)
- [Docker Hub bitnami/kubectl tags](https://hub.docker.com/r/bitnami/kubectl/tags)

Step 3: Fix Missing 'Operate' Tab (Troubleshoot)
If the "Operate" tab is missing in the Web UI, you may need to manually assign the Owner role to your user via the Rails console.

1. Shell into the crewai-web pod:

kubectl exec --stdin --tty deploy/crewai-web -n crewai -- /bin/bash

2. Start the Rails console:

bin/rails c

3. Define the role assignment function (paste this code block):

def assign_owner_role(user_email)
  user = User.find_by(email: user_email)
  organization = Organization.find_by(name: "Default")
  owner_role = organization.roles.find_by(name: "Owner")
  membership = organization.memberships.find_by(user_id: user.id)
  membership.update!(role_id: owner_role.id)
end

4. Run the assignment function (replace with your user email):

assign_owner_role("nathan.booth@konecta.com")

| Step | Description |

| 3/4 | Add platform owner |

> AGENT

I inlined the Ruby code directly rather than defining and calling the function. The logic is equivalent:

```ruby
# My implementation (inline):
user = User.find_by(email: '$OWNER_EMAIL')
organization = Organization.find_by(name: 'Default')
owner_role = organization.roles.find_by(name: 'Owner')
membership = organization.memberships.find_by(user_id: user.id)
membership.update!(role_id: owner_role.id)
```

This does exactly what `assign_owner_role("$OWNER_EMAIL")` would do. Since we're only calling it once, inlining is cleaner for a shell script context.

> AGENT

Done. The job now checks for the `application-installed` ConfigMap first:

**Flow:**
1. Check if `application-installed` ConfigMap exists → skip if yes
2. Wait for crewai-web deployment to be ready
3. Run the 4 setup steps
4. ConfigMap gets created at sync-wave 15 (after job completes)

**Benefits:**
- Faster check (no need to exec into pod and query Rails)
- Cleaner marker for successful installation
- Deployment wait is skipped on subsequent syncs

Based on the search results, here's what I found about the **d3fk/kubectl** Docker image and Alpine shell/bash considerations:

## d3fk/kubectl Docker Image

The d3fk/kubectl is a super lightweight container with only the Kubectl official binary plus a default non-root user (~44MB). It is made from scratch (downloaded from googleapis through alpine image and directly poured from alpine into scratch), prebuilt on Docker Hub with "automated build" as multi-arch.

### Key Characteristics:
- The d3fk/kubectl:latest multi-arch image available from Docker Hub is made with automated build auto-triggered every day, ensuring you have the last stable version available of Kubectl within 24H max after its release.
- This container is useful to manage Kubernetes clusters from anywhere like simple docker containers or from other k8s pods, jobs, cronjobs. It can be used for CI/CD or as your main Kubectl command.

### Important Note About Shell Access:
Since d3fk/kubectl is built **from scratch** (not Alpine-based in the final image), it contains only the kubectl binary - **no shell is included**. This is different from Alpine-based images.

## Alpine Linux and Bash

Alpine Linux-based container images do not have bash installed. Alpine uses the busybox provided ash shell (which is basically a symbolic link to /bin/busybox).

Alpine is an open-source and simple Linux distribution system. It uses a busybox by default. The busybox provides a very minimal shell environment called ash.

### Alternatives with Bash Included:
If you need kubectl with bash shell access, consider these alternatives:

1. **alpine/k8s** - Includes kubectl, kustomize, helm, and general tools such as bash, curl, jq, yq, etc.

2. **dtzar/helm-kubectl** - This lightweight alpine docker image provides kubectl and helm binaries for working with a Kubernetes cluster.

3. **beli/kubectl-shell** - Alpine based image with bash, kubectl, Helm and some CLI tools.

name: Checkout code\n        uses: actions/checkout@v4\n\n      - name: Configure GCP Auth\n        id: gcp-auth-config\n        run: |\n          PROJECT_NUMBER=\"${{ vars.GCP_PROJECT_NUMBER }}\"\n          SERVICE_NAME=\"${{ vars.SERVICE_NAME }}\"\n\n          if [ -z \"$PROJECT_NUMBER\" ] || [ -z \"$SERVICE_NAME\" ]; then\n            echo \"::error::Missing required environment variables.\"\n            echo \"::error::Set GCP_PROJECT_NUMBER and SERVICE_NAME as GitHub Environment variables for '${{ inputs.environment }}'.\"\n            exit 1\n          fi\n\n          ENV=\"${{ inputs.environment }}\"\n          POOL_ID=\"github-${SERVICE_NAME}-${ENV}\"\n          PROVIDER=\"projects/${PROJECT_NUMBER}/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/${POOL_ID}/providers/github-provider\"\n          SA=\"${POOL_ID}@kd-ix-eur-${ENV}-gke.iam.gserviceaccount.com\"\n\n          echo \"provider_id=${PROVIDER}\" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT\n          echo \"service_account=${SA}\" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT\n\n      - name: Authenticate to GCP\n        uses: google-github-actions/auth@v2\n        with:\n          workload_identity_provider: ${{ steps.gcp-auth-config.outputs.provider_id }}\n          service_account: ${{ steps.gcp-auth-config.outputs.service_account }}\n\n      - name: Setup Cloud SDK\n        uses: google-github-actions/setup-gcloud@v2\n\n      - name: Get GKE credentials\n        run: |\n          ENV=\"${{ inputs.environment }}\"\n          gcloud container clusters get-credentials \"kd-ix-eur-${ENV}-gke\" \\\n            --region europe-west1 \\\n            --project \"kd-ix-eur-${ENV}-gke\"\n\n      - name: Determine namespace\n        id: namespace\n        run: |\n          ENV=\"${{ inputs.environment }}\"\n          if [ \"$ENV\" == \"dev\" ]; then\n            echo \"namespace=crewai\" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT\n          else\n            echo \"namespace=crewai-${ENV}\" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT\n          fi\n\n      - name: Check if already configured\n        id: check\n        run: |\n          NAMESPACE=\"${{ steps.namespace.outputs.namespace }}\"\n          echo \"==============================================\"\n          echo \"Checking if platform is already configured...\"\n          echo \"==============================================\"\n\n          INTERNAL_ORG_EXISTS=$(kubectl exec deploy/crewai-web -n \"$NAMESPACE\" -- \\\n            bundle exec rails runner \"puts Organization.where(internal: true).exists?\" 2>/dev/null || echo \"false\")\n\n          if [ \"$INTERNAL_ORG_EXISTS\" = \"true\" ]; then\n            echo \"already_configured=true\" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT\n            echo \"::warning::Platform already configured - internal organization exists\"\n          else\n            echo \"already_configured=false\" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT\n            echo \"Platform not yet configured - proceeding with setup\"\n          fi\n\n      - name: Install internal organization\n        if: steps.check.outputs.already_configured != 'true'\n        run: |\n          NAMESPACE=\"${{ steps.namespace.outputs.namespace }}\"\n\n          echo \"==============================================\"\n          echo \"Step 1/4: Installing internal organization\"\n          echo \"==============================================\"\n\n          kubectl exec deploy/crewai-web -n \"$NAMESPACE\" -- \\\n            bundle exec rake studio:install_internal_organization\n\n          echo \"Internal organization created\"\n\n      - name: Setup default permissions\n        if: steps.check.outputs.already_configured != 'true'\n        run: |\n          NAMESPACE=\"${{ steps.namespace.outputs.namespace }}\"\n\n          echo \"==============================================\"\n          echo \"Step 2/4: Setting up default permissions\"\n          echo \"==============================================\"\n\n          kubectl exec deploy/crewai-web -n \"$NAMESPACE\" -- \\\n            bundle exec rake factory:setup_permissions_defaults\n\n          echo \"Default permissions configured\"\n\n      - name: Add platform owner\n        if: steps.check.outputs.already_configured != 'true'\n        run: |\n          NAMESPACE=\"${{ steps.namespace.outputs.namespace }}\"\n          OWNER_ORG_ID=\"${{ inputs.owner_org_id }}\"\n          OWNER_EMAIL=\"${{ inputs.owner_email }}\"\n\n          echo \"==============================================\"\n          echo \"Step 3/4: Adding platform owner\"\n          echo \"==============================================\"\n          echo \"Organization ID: $OWNER_ORG_ID\"\n          echo \"Owner Email: $OWNER_EMAIL\"\n\n          kubectl exec deploy/crewai-web -n \"$NAMESPACE\" -- \\\n            bundle exec rake \"factory:add_owner[$OWNER_ORG_ID,$OWNER_EMAIL]\"\n\n          echo \"Platform owner added: $OWNER_EMAIL\"\n\n      - name: Assign Owner role to platform owner\n        if: steps.check.outputs.already_configured != 'true'\n        run: |\n          NAMESPACE=\"${{ steps.namespace.outputs.namespace }}\"\n          OWNER_EMAIL=\"${{ inputs.owner_email }}\"\n\n          echo \"==============================================\"\n          echo \"Step 4/4: Assigning Owner role to platform owner\"\n          echo \"==============================================\"\n\n          kubectl exec deploy/crewai-web -n \"$NAMESPACE\" -- \\\n            bundle exec rails runner \"\n              user = User.find_by(email: '$OWNER_EMAIL')\n              organization = Organization.find_by(name: 'Default')\n              owner_role = organization.roles.find_by(name: 'Owner')\n              membership = organization.memberships.find_by(user_id: user.id)\n              membership.update!(role_id: owner_role.id)\n              puts 'Owner role assigned successfully'\n            \"\n\n          echo \"Owner role assigned to: $OWNER_EMAIL\"\n\n      - Install internal organization\" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY\n            echo \"2. Setup default permissions\" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY\n            echo \"3. Add platform owner\" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY\n            echo \"4. Assign Owner role to platform owner\" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY\n          fi\n"

The auth fields are empty. The user was created by the rake task without SSO provider info. When you login via WorkOS, it tries to create a new user because it can't match by provider/uid.

Check the User columns:
```bash
kubectl exec deploy/crewai-web -n crewai -- bundle exec rails runner "puts User.column_names.sort.join(', ')"
```

Then we can update the user with the correct provider info. What's the email you're logging in with from WorkOS?

> AGENT

Since `AUTH_PROVIDER: "local"` is set, the app uses local auth, not WorkOS SSO.

The simplest fix is to delete the rake-created user and login fresh - the local auth flow will create the user properly:

```bash
kubectl exec deploy/crewai-web -n crewai -- bundle exec rails runner "User.find_by(email: 'kix-platform@konecta.com')&.destroy!"
```

Then login via the app - it will create a new user. After that, run steps 3 & 4 again to add owner + assign role:

```bash
kubectl exec deploy/crewai-web -n crewai -- bundle exec rake "factory:add_owner[2,kix-platform@konecta.com]"
```

> AGENT

Done. The workflow now has a verification step that runs when the organization already exists. Here's what it does:

**When `already_configured=true`:**
1. Checks if the user exists
2. Checks if the user has a membership in the Default org
3. Checks if the membership has the Owner role
4. **Auto-fixes** if the user has a membership but wrong role

**Outputs:**
- `OWNER_OK` - All good, owner permissions verified
- `USER_NOT_FOUND` - User needs to log in first (warning)
- `NO_MEMBERSHIP` - User exists but no org membership (warning with manual fix suggestion)
- `WRONG_ROLE` - User has membership but wrong role → **automatically fixed**

> AGENT

Yes, Kubernetes DNS supports cross-namespace service resolution. Use the fully qualified name:

```
<service-name>.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local
```

Or the shorter form:
```
<service-name>.<namespace>
```

**Examples:**
- Same namespace: `cloud-sql-proxy` (just the service name)
- Different namespace: `cloud-sql-proxy.crewai` or `cloud-sql-proxy.crewai.svc.cluster.local`

**However**, if resolution isn't working, check:

1. **NetworkPolicy** - May be blocking DNS egress (port 53 UDP/TCP to `kube-system`)
2. **Service exists** - `kubectl get svc -n <namespace>`
3. **CoreDNS running** - `kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l k8s-app=kube-dns`

Are you having a specific resolution issue? I can help debug if you share what you're trying to reach from where.

If so, the DNS name would be:

<service-name>.litellm-dev
```

For example, if the LiteLLM service is called `litellm`:
```
litellm.litellm-dev
```

> AGENT

Added egress rule for LiteLLM. The change allows crewai pods to reach port 4000 in the `litellm` namespace:

```yaml
# Allow traffic to LiteLLM in litellm namespace
- to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          kubernetes.io/metadata.name: litellm
  ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 4000
```

**Note:** The `litellm` namespace needs to have the label `kubernetes.io/metadata.name: litellm` (this is automatically added by Kubernetes 1.21+).

name: Checkout code\n        uses: actions/checkout@v4\n\n      - name: Configure GCP Auth\n        id: gcp-auth-config\n        run: |\n          PROJECT_NUMBER=\"${{ vars.GCP_PROJECT_NUMBER }}\"\n          SERVICE_NAME=\"${{ vars.SERVICE_NAME }}\"\n\n          if [ -z \"$PROJECT_NUMBER\" ] || [ -z \"$SERVICE_NAME\" ]; then\n            echo \"::error::Missing required environment variables.\"\n            echo \"::error::Set GCP_PROJECT_NUMBER and SERVICE_NAME as GitHub Environment variables for '${{ inputs.environment }}'.\"\n            exit 1\n          fi\n\n          ENV=\"${{ inputs.environment }}\"\n          POOL_ID=\"github-${SERVICE_NAME}-${ENV}\"\n          PROVIDER=\"projects/${PROJECT_NUMBER}/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/${POOL_ID}/providers/github-provider\"\n          SA=\"${POOL_ID}@kd-ix-eur-${ENV}-gke.iam.gserviceaccount.com\"\n\n          echo \"provider_id=${PROVIDER}\" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT\n          echo \"service_account=${SA}\" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT\n\n      - name: Authenticate to GCP\n        uses: google-github-actions/auth@v2\n        with:\n          workload_identity_provider: ${{ steps.gcp-auth-config.outputs.provider_id }}\n          service_account: ${{ steps.gcp-auth-config.outputs.service_account }}\n\n      - name: Setup Cloud SDK\n        uses: google-github-actions/setup-gcloud@v2\n\n      - name: Install GKE auth plugin\n        run: |\n          gcloud components install gke-gcloud-auth-plugin --quiet\n\n      - name: Get GKE credentials\n        run: |\n          ENV=\"${{ inputs.environment }}\"\n          gcloud container clusters get-credentials \"kd-ix-eur-${ENV}-cluster\" \\\n            --region europe-west1 \\\n            --project \"kd-ix-eur-${ENV}-gke\"\n\n      - name: Determine namespace\n        id: namespace\n        run: |\n          ENV=\"${{ inputs.environment }}\"\n          if [ \"$ENV\" == \"dev\" ]; then\n            echo \"namespace=crewai\" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT\n          else\n            echo \"namespace=crewai-${ENV}\" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT\n          fi\n\n      - name: Check if already configured\n        id: check\n        run: |\n          NAMESPACE=\"${{ steps.namespace.outputs.namespace }}\"\n          echo \"==============================================\"\n          echo \"Checking if platform is already configured...\"\n          echo \"==============================================\"\n\n          # Check for 'Default' organization (created by setup process)\n          # Use tail -1 to get only the last line (Rails warnings go to stdout)\n          DEFAULT_ORG_EXISTS=$(kubectl exec deploy/crewai-web -n \"$NAMESPACE\" -- \\\n            bundle exec rails runner \"puts Organization.exists?(name: 'Default')\" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 || echo \"false\")\n\n          if [ \"$DEFAULT_ORG_EXISTS\" = \"true\" ]; then\n            echo \"already_configured=true\" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT\n            echo \"::warning::Platform already configured - Default organization exists\"\n          else\n            echo \"already_configured=false\" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT\n            echo \"Platform not yet configured - proceeding with setup\"\n          fi\n\n      - name: Verify owner permissions (existing setup)\n        if: steps.check.outputs.already_configured == 'true'\n        run: |\n          NAMESPACE=\"${{ steps.namespace.outputs.namespace }}\"\n          OWNER_EMAIL=\"${{ inputs.owner_email }}\"\n\n          echo \"==============================================\"\n          echo \"Verifying owner permissions for existing setup\"\n          echo \"==============================================\"\n          echo \"Checking: $OWNER_EMAIL\"\n\n          # Check if user exists, has membership in Default org, and has Owner role\n          RESULT=$(kubectl exec deploy/crewai-web -n \"$NAMESPACE\" -- \\\n            bundle exec rails runner \"\n              user = User.find_by(email: '${OWNER_EMAIL}')\n              unless user\n                puts 'USER_NOT_FOUND'\n                exit\n              end\n              org = Organization.find_by(name: 'Default')\n              unless org\n                puts 'ORG_NOT_FOUND'\n                exit\n              end\n              membership = org.memberships.find_by(user_id: user.id)\n              unless membership\n                puts 'NO_MEMBERSHIP'\n                exit\n              end\n              owner_role = org.roles.find_by(name: 'Owner')\n              if membership.role_id == owner_role&.id\n                puts 'OWNER_OK'\n              else\n                puts 'WRONG_ROLE'\n              end\n            \" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 || echo \"ERROR\")\n\n          echo \"Result: $RESULT\"\n\n          case \"$RESULT\" in\n            \"OWNER_OK\")\n              echo \"✅ Owner permissions verified for $OWNER_EMAIL\"\n              ;;\n            \"USER_NOT_FOUND\")\n              echo \"::warning::User $OWNER_EMAIL not found - they may need to log in first\"\n              ;;\n            \"NO_MEMBERSHIP\")\n              echo \"::warning::User $OWNER_EMAIL exists but has no membership in Default org\"\n              echo \"Run factory:add_owner manually to add membership\"\n              ;;\n            \"WRONG_ROLE\")\n              echo \"::warning::User $OWNER_EMAIL has membership but not Owner role - fixing...\"\n              kubectl exec deploy/crewai-web -n \"$NAMESPACE\" -- \\\n                bundle exec rails runner \"user = User.find_by!(email: '${OWNER_EMAIL}'); org = Organization.find_by!(name: 'Default'); role = org.roles.find_by!(name: 'Owner'); membership = org.memberships.find_by!(user_id: user.id); membership.update!(role_id: role.id); puts 'Owner role assigned successfully'\"\n              echo \"✅ Owner role assigned to $OWNER_EMAIL\"\n              ;;\n            *)\n              echo \"::error::Failed to verify permissions: $RESULT\"\n              ;;\n          esac\n\n      - name: Install internal organization\n        if: steps.check.outputs.already_configured != 'true'\n        run: |\n          NAMESPACE=\"${{ steps.namespace.outputs.namespace }}\"\n\n          echo \"==============================================\"\n          echo \"Step 1/4: Installing internal organization\"\n          echo \"==============================================\"\n\n          kubectl exec deploy/crewai-web -n \"$NAMESPACE\" -- \\\n            bundle exec rake studio:install_internal_organization\n\n          echo \"Internal organization created\"\n\n      - name: Setup default permissions\n        if: steps.check.outputs.already_configured != 'true'\n        run: |\n          NAMESPACE=\"${{ steps.namespace.outputs.namespace }}\"\n\n          echo \"==============================================\"\n          echo \"Step 2/4: Setting up default permissions\"\n          echo \"==============================================\"\n\n          kubectl exec deploy/crewai-web -n \"$NAMESPACE\" -- \\\n            bundle exec rake factory:setup_permissions_defaults\n\n          echo \"Default permissions configured\"\n\n      - name: Add platform owner\n        if: steps.check.outputs.already_configured != 'true'\n        run: |\n          NAMESPACE=\"${{ steps.namespace.outputs.namespace }}\"\n          OWNER_ORG_ID=\"${{ inputs.owner_org_id }}\"\n          OWNER_EMAIL=\"${{ inputs.owner_email }}\"\n\n          echo \"==============================================\"\n          echo \"Step 3/4: Adding platform owner\"\n          echo \"==============================================\"\n          echo \"Organization ID: $OWNER_ORG_ID\"\n          echo \"Owner Email: $OWNER_EMAIL\"\n\n          kubectl exec deploy/crewai-web -n \"$NAMESPACE\" -- \\\n            bundle exec rake \"factory:add_owner[$OWNER_ORG_ID,$OWNER_EMAIL]\"\n\n          echo \"Platform owner added: $OWNER_EMAIL\"\n\n      - name: Assign Owner role to platform owner\n        if: steps.check.outputs.already_configured != 'true'\n        run: |\n          NAMESPACE=\"${{ steps.namespace.outputs.namespace }}\"\n          OWNER_EMAIL=\"${{ inputs.owner_email }}\"\n\n          echo \"==============================================\"\n          echo \"Step 4/4: Assigning Owner role to platform owner\"\n          echo \"==============================================\"\n          kubectl exec deploy/crewai-web -n \"$NAMESPACE\" -- \\\n            bundle exec rails runner \"user = User.find_by!(email: '${OWNER_EMAIL}'); org = Organization.find_by!(name: 'Default'); role = org.roles.find_by!(name: 'Owner'); membership = org.memberships.find_by!(user_id: user.id); membership.update!(role_id: role.id); puts 'Owner role assigned successfully'\"\n          echo \"Owner role assigned to: $OWNER_EMAIL\"\n\n      - name: Summary\n        if: always()\n        run: |\n          echo \"## Organization Initial Setup\" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY\n          echo \"\" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY\n          echo \"**Environment:** ${{ inputs.environment }}\" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY\n          echo \"**Namespace:** ${{ steps.namespace.outputs.namespace }}\" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY\n          echo \"**Owner Org ID:** ${{ inputs.owner_org_id }}\" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY\n          echo \"**Owner Email:** ${{ inputs.owner_email }}\" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY\n          echo \"\" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY\n\n          if [ \"${{ steps.check.outputs.already_configured }}\" == \"true\" ]; then\n            echo \"**Status:** Already configured - verified owner permissions\" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY\n            echo \"\" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY\n            echo \"Owner permissions for **${{ inputs.owner_email }}** were checked and corrected if needed.\" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY\n          else\n            echo \"### Steps Completed\" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY\n            echo \"1. Install internal organization\" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY\n            echo \"2. Setup default permissions\" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY\n            echo \"3. Add platform owner\" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY\n            echo \"4. Assign Owner role to platform owner\" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY\n          fi\n"
}

> AGENT

The NetworkPolicy is applied to the **crewai namespace** (via the helper `crewai-gateway.crewaiNamespace`).

Key details:
- **Namespace:** `crewai` (from [values.yaml](environments/dev/helm/crewai/values.yaml#L24): `crewai.namespace: "crewai"`)
- **Target pods:** `app.kubernetes.io/name: crewai-platform` (from values `networkPolicy.podSelector`)
- **LiteLLM egress:** Lines 103-105 include the `additionalEgress` rules (including the LiteLLM rule we added)

The policy selects pods with label `app.kubernetes.io/name: crewai-platform` in the `crewai` namespace and allows egress to:
- DNS (kube-system + NodeLocal cache)
- Kubernetes API server
- GKE metadata server (Workload Identity)
- External IPs on port 443
- cloud-sql-proxy on port 5432
- litellm namespace on port 4000 (newly added)

> AGENT

Found it! The **litellm service exposes port 80**, not 4000:

```
litellm-dev   ClusterIP   10.20.7.207   <none>        80/TCP,9090/TCP
```

The service maps **port 80 → pod port 4000**.

Our NetworkPolicy allows egress to port 4000, but you need to connect on **port 80** (the service port).

**Two options:**

**Option 1: Change the URL to use port 80:**
```
http://litellm-dev.litellm:80/v1
# or just
http://litellm-dev.litellm/v1
```

**Option 2: Update the NetworkPolicy to allow port 80:**

> TOOL

  "new_string": "    # Allow traffic to LiteLLM in litellm namespace (service port 80)\n    - to:\n        - namespaceSelector:\n            matchLabels:\n              kubernetes.io/metadata.name: litellm\n      ports:\n        - protocol: TCP\n          port: 80"
}
```

> AGENT

The network policy shows port 80 to the litellm namespace. That **should** be sufficient because:

- You connect to the **service** on port 80
- The service translates port 80 → pod port 4000

However, in GKE Dataplane v2, the network policy might be evaluated **after** the service NAT, meaning it sees traffic going to the pod on port 4000, not the service on port 80.

**Try adding both ports** to be safe:

> TOOL

tool_use Edit
id: toolu_013hS9eTUNMzx6KSCp5ceTP5
```json
{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/home/nathan_booth/code/konecta/konecta-tic/kix-services-crewai/environments/dev/helm/crewai/values.yaml",
  "old_string": "    # Allow traffic to LiteLLM in litellm namespace (service port 80)\n    - to:\n        - namespaceSelector:\n            matchLabels:\n              kubernetes.io/metadata.name: litellm\n      ports:\n        - protocol: TCP\n          port: 80",
  "new_string": "    # Allow traffic to LiteLLM in litellm namespace\n    # Port 80: service port (pre-NAT)\n    # Port 4000: pod port (post-NAT, for Dataplane v2)\n    - to:\n        - namespaceSelector:\n            matchLabels:\n              kubernetes.io/metadata.name: litellm\n      ports:\n        - protocol: TCP\n          port: 80\n        - protocol: TCP\n          port: 4000"
}
```

> AGENT

Created **PR #91**: https://github.com/konecta-ix-services/kix-services-crewai/pull/91

This adds port 4000 alongside port 80 for the LiteLLM egress rule. GKE Dataplane v2 (Cilium) may evaluate network policies **after** service NAT, meaning it sees traffic destined for the pod port (4000) rather than the service port (80).

Once merged and synced by ArgoCD, test with:
```bash
kubectl exec -it deploy/crewai-web -n crewai -- curl -v http://litellm-dev.litellm:80/health
```
